components.description: A lightweight sidecar or middleware component that intercepts agent interactions. It continuously tracks and aggregates real-time metrics: elapsed time, token counts (input/output), number of tool calls, and estimated monetary cost.
components.name: Resource Monitor

components.description: An RL agent (e.g., using PPO or DQN) that learns optimal budget allocation strategies. It takes the current state (task complexity, remaining budget, historical performance) and outputs a policy update (e.g., 'tighten limits' or 'relax limits').
components.name: Budget Policy Learner

components.description: A synchronous gatekeeper that sits between the agent and the LLM/Tools. It evaluates the current action against the active policy from the Learner. If a limit is breached, it can interrupt the agent, request a summary, or switch to a cheaper model.
components.name: Decision Engine

data_flow: 1. Agent initiates an action (LLM call or Tool use).
2. Decision Engine checks current resource usage against the active Policy.
3. If within limits, action proceeds; Resource Monitor logs the delta.
4. Resource Monitor sends usage data to the Budget Policy Learner.
5. Learner updates its internal state and potentially refines the Policy based on reward signals (e.g., task success vs. cost).
6. Updated Policy is pushed to the Decision Engine for the next step.

trade_offs_analysis.chosen_approach: Adaptive Budget Controller with Reinforcement Learning
cons: Requires a training phase with simulated or historical data.
Risk of non-deterministic behavior during early learning stages.
pros: High adaptability to varying task complexities.
Optimizes for long-term efficiency rather than static thresholds.
Scalable across different agent types and environments.
trade_offs_analysis.rejection_reason: Lacks flexibility; static thresholds lead to poor performance in dynamic enterprise environments where task difficulty varies significantly.

specification.context: Part of the 'From RAG to Governed Enterprise Agents' series. Addresses the critical engineering challenge of preventing runaway costs and latency in autonomous AI agents.
key_metrics: Tool call success rate vs. budget consumed
specification.problem_statement: Autonomous agents operating in enterprise environments face unbounded resource consumption risks (time, tokens, tool calls, monetary spend). Static rule-based limits fail to adapt to dynamic task complexities, leading to either premature termination of complex tasks or excessive spending on simple ones.
specification.solution_summary: An adaptive budget controller leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL) to dynamically adjust resource allocation policies based on real-time performance feedback, balancing cost-efficiency with task completion quality.
specification.title: Agent Budget Controller: Adaptive Resource Governance

takeaway: Static rules are insufficient for dynamic AI agents. By applying Reinforcement Learning to resource management, we can create agents that are not only intelligent but also economically and operationally self-governing, ensuring sustainable enterprise adoption.
